summary: Work through Safe Sets as Conditional Permission.

sections: Kinetic barrier certificates and relative degree

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Safe Sets as Conditional Permission**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Safety Enforcement, § Safe Sets as Conditional Permission
blocks.md: Once gravitational bias torque is counted, the descending arm analyzed in a later section requires … of tool travel to brake to a complete stop, and this stopping distance scales quadratically with approach speed. A clearance margin that guarantees safety at one velocity fails completely at a higher velocity. The runtime safety enforcer therefore requires a joint predicate over position and velocity that it can evaluate synchronously on every tick of the control clock.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Kinetic barrier matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A control barrier function makes its safe set forward invariant only if every admitted input keeps hdot >= -alpha(h), and a barrier on raw distance has relative degree two in torque, so the barrier must carry the cost to stop.

questions.q: The section **Safe Sets as Conditional Permission** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A least-change projection passes a safe proposal untouched and projects a violating one onto the barrier boundary, keeping learned competence, while a structurally invalid proposal is vetoed rather than corrected.
When contact is the task the kinetic barrier admits only zero speed, so an energy-tank passivity barrier and a separately qualified force channel replace clearance as the margin.

Safety functions, not components, are graded by SIL or by a Performance Level that combines category, MTTFd, diagnostic coverage, and common-cause defenses; the standards set the required level for each function of this machine, and only the functions selected for a rating carry the formal claim.

A control barrier function makes its safe set forward invariant only if every admitted input keeps hdot >= -alpha(h), and a barrier on raw distance has relative degree two in torque, so the barrier must carry the cost to stop.
